global_limits: Evidence only. No production content, review gate, reference, note, expression, source registry or runtime is changed.
All proposals require a separate independent decision. No human, specialist, expression, morphology, media, module or release acceptance is claimed.
Difficulty is an editorial teaching proposal. Literal Oxford cefr and fkcefr attributes, missing labels, Collins B1+ values and disagreements remain explicit.
Whole-entry hazard, collect, notify, postpone and verify holds remain exact. All 17 inherited expression holds and every containing Foundation02 expression remain exact.
Source consultation is not an asset license or acquisition. No publisher definitions, examples, exercises, illustrations, audio or page bodies are imported.

proposed_fields.definition: Damaged or unable to work as intended.
proposed_fields.example: The handle on this case is broken.

entries.selected_sense: The adjective for a damaged or nonfunctioning object, illustrated by a case handle.
entries.language_rationale: Retain the original concise definition and concrete handle example. They fit the selected object sense without importing promise, relationship or emotional meanings.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Retain editorial A2 on Oxford selected adjective sense 1 cefr a2. Collins A2 belongs to its past-participle cross-reference, not to a separately graded adjective; the relevant British adjective senses show no level.
entries.excluded_scope: Broken promises, relationships, interrupted sleep or lines, limited language proficiency and a demoralized person are separate. Break as a verb and its other inflections are not accepted through this adjective.
entries.context_boundary: Foundation02.06 retains report/fault/replace and its exact pending expression. Broken seals, glass and a broken link are distinct context uses; this research creates no bindings or content approval for them.
entries.proposed_note: Retain the original object adjective and editorial A2. No expression, morphology or asset gate is accepted.

proposed_fields.definition: Needing attention or action without delay.
proposed_fields.example: This message is urgent because the delivery leaves shortly.

entries.selected_sense: A matter needing prompt attention or action, in an ordinary delivery-message context.
entries.language_rationale: The original revision replaces very soon with without delay to express the selected need for prompt action. Retain the original delivery-message example.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Propose editorial B2 from Oxford selected sense 1 cefr b2. Collins labels its selected sense B1+ literally. The difference remains explicit; this is not a consensus claim or a conversion of B1+.
entries.excluded_scope: An insistent voice or expression is a separate sense. Clinical urgency, triage thresholds and response-time duties are not established by this ordinary message example.
entries.context_boundary: Foundation02.05 remains exact and pending with concern, solution and unintegrated resolve. Caregiving07.04 concerns urgent medical assessment; lexical consultation does not approve that clinical claim or bind this lexeme there.
entries.proposed_note: Proposed original wording and editorial B2 for prompt attention. Collins B1+ is preserved as a distinct observed label.

proposed_fields.definition: Difficult to understand or not stated precisely.
proposed_fields.example: The instructions are unclear about the start time.

entries.selected_sense: Wording or information that is not expressed clearly enough to understand precisely.
entries.language_rationale: Retain the original wording and start-time example. They describe unclear information rather than declaring that a person lacks understanding.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Propose editorial B1 on Oxford selected sense 1 cefr b1 and its selected B1 topic. Collins COBUILD unknown-or-uncertain sense 1 is B2 and its broader British ambiguous/not-definite definition is ungraded. Their scopes and labels are not collapsed.
entries.excluded_scope: A person unsure about something is a separate sense. Clear, clearly, clarify and clarification remain distinct forms and identities; no inference about morphology or language teaching is accepted.
entries.context_boundary: No selected focus expression currently binds this entry. OfficeAdmin05.07 is an inherited whole-expression hold; retail use-by-date and commercial-relationship contexts remain unscored and pending.
entries.proposed_note: Retain the original information adjective with editorial B1; preserve Collins B2 and the separate person-uncertainty sense.

proposed_fields.definition: Unlikely to cause harm or put someone in danger.
proposed_fields.example: The team asked whether the route was safe to use.

entries.selected_sense: A thing, route or activity unlikely to cause harm, as a question about using a route.
entries.language_rationale: The authored definition selects the route-not-causing-harm sense and removes the unestablished unacceptable-risk criterion and the separate protected-person sense. The original question example does not guarantee a route is safe.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Retain editorial A2 on Oxford selected sense 2 cefr a2 and Collins physical-danger sense 1 A2. The lexical label does not establish a professional safety threshold.
entries.excluded_scope: Protected or unharmed people, secure possessions, reliable predictions, lack of controversy and the safe container noun are distinct. This is not a risk-acceptance standard, route assessment or guarantee.
entries.context_boundary: Foundation02.09 remains exact with its domain gate pending. Hospitality room safe and accounting safe are container nouns, not instances of this adjective. Safely, safety and safeguards remain separate.
entries.proposed_note: Proposed original route/object adjective definition with editorial A2; all safety-domain judgments remain pending.

proposed_fields.definition: Presenting a risk of harm in the situation.
proposed_fields.example: The worker reported an unsafe storage area.

entries.selected_sense: A thing, place or activity that may cause harm, illustrated by a reported storage area.
entries.language_rationale: Retain the original definition and reported-area example. They fit the dangerous-place sense without approving an inspection or defining the conditions that make an area unsafe.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Propose B1 only as an editorial teaching judgment for the concrete dangerous-place adjective in a simple report. Oxford selected sense 1 has neither cefr nor fkcefr, and Collins displays no selected level. Cambridge was inaccessible. There is no observed publisher certification for B1; the independent reviewer may hold this proposal if a direct level source is required.
entries.excluded_scope: A person exposed to danger and the British legal meaning of an unsafe conviction are separate. No threshold, hazard evaluation, work instruction or morphology approval follows from the proposal.
entries.context_boundary: Foundation02.09 remains exact and domain pending with safe and procedure. This is the sole selected surface/focus expression. No additional scored binding is proposed.
entries.proposed_note: Retain the original dangerous-place wording and propose editorial B1 without a publisher-level claim. Domain review remains pending.

proposed_fields.definition: An event at work, especially one that is unusual or causes a problem.
proposed_fields.example: The supervisor recorded the incident after speaking with the team.

entries.selected_sense: An individual event, narrowed by this lexeme to the workplace and often unusual or problematic.
entries.language_rationale: The authored definition removes the unsupported universal requirement for attention or recording. The original example reports a supervisor recording one event; it does not define a recording duty.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Propose editorial B2 on Oxford ordinary-event sense 1 cefr b2 and Collins selected noun B2. Collins formal register is preserved.
entries.excluded_scope: A violent event and a diplomatic clash are separately described senses. Incident forms, IT incident response and domain-specific reporting classifications or duties are not approved by the ordinary event meaning.
entries.context_boundary: Foundation02.10 remains exact with the hazard whole-entry hold and its domain gate pending. Eleven external incident uses include form compounds and IT/service response contexts; none gains a selected binding or reporting approval.
entries.proposed_note: Propose original workplace-event definition and editorial B2; retain the narrative recording example without creating a duty.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Propose editorial B2 on Collins exact countable worrying-fact/situation sense 3 B2. Oxford worry sense 1 cefr b2 is related noun evidence; its important-matter sense 3 is separate and is not silently substituted for the exact countable sense.
entries.excluded_scope: The verb meaning is about, concern for another person, a responsibility or priority, a company and going concern are separate. Safeguarding, security and clinical compounds need their own context decisions.
entries.context_boundary: Foundation02.05 remains exact and pending. Many surface concerns are verbs meaning is about; the other external uses span ordinary worries and specialist concerns. No selected noun binding, specialist meaning or reporting practice is added.
entries.proposed_note: Proposed original countable worrying-matter definition and editorial B2. Oxford related emotional noun evidence and Collins exact countable evidence remain distinguishable.
